title: TS SDK: fluent AsyncIterable <-> ReadableStream conversion utility
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Provide a small, well-typed TypeScript utility and migration examples that make converting between AsyncIterable<T> and Web Streams (ReadableStream) easy and ergonomic across Node, Deno, and browser runtimes. Motivation: teams keep hitting edge cases when bridging SDK streaming outputs (AsyncIterable) to browser ReadableStream consumers and vice versa: backpressure semantics, cancellation propagation, error mapping, and runtime differences. This ticket designs and implements a "fluent" conversion helper that preserves cancellation/backpressure, supports teeing and transform pipelines, and documents recommended patterns for retries and resumability.

Scope:
- Implement two one-file utilities: asyncIterableToReadableStream<T>(iterable, opts) and readableStreamToAsyncIterable<T>(stream, opts).
- Provide small ergonomic wrappers for common patterns: passthroughTransform, chunkFraming, and earlyFlush for small-chunk low-latency workloads.
- Ensure the utilities propagate cancellation (AbortSignal), map errors consistently to SDK error types, and surface upstream retry tokens for resume.
- Add polyfills/adapters for Node 18+ (native ReadableStream), Node <18 (stream.Readable adapter), Deno, and modern browsers.
- Add test matrix covering Node/Deno/Browser, backpressure scenarios, double-consume detection, tee() semantics, and network-interruption retry simulation.
- Create migration examples in docs and a short guide that shows < 10-line conversions for app code.

Design considerations & trade-offs:
- Backpressure: Use the ReadableStream queuingStrategy default in browsers and hook pull/flush callbacks to pull from the AsyncIterator only when consumer requests data. For Node older runtimes we will emulate pull semantics using async iteration and controlled push to readable buffer.
- Cancellation: Accept an optional AbortSignal in both helpers; cancellation should close the other side cleanly and surface a consistent CancellationError that integrates with SDK retry logic.
- Multiple consumers: Warn and reject patterns that try to attach multiple concurrent async consumers to a single ReadableStream unless user explicitly calls tee() or the helper is passed tee: true.
- Performance: Avoid per-token micro-allocations in hot paths; provide a small internal buffer size option (default 8) and allow users to tune for throughput vs latency.

Examples (short):
- AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream (browser):
  const rs = asyncIterableToReadableStream(myAsyncGen(), { signal: controller.signal });
  // can pipe to native browser APIs: response.body = rs;

- ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable (node):
  for await (const chunk of readableStreamToAsyncIterable(fetchRes.body)) {
    handle(chunk);
  }

- Retry integration note: helpers will emit a serializable resume token on the conversion when available (opts.resumeTokenHook = token => ...) so retry middleware can persist a resume point between attempts.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics are listed separately below.
acceptance_criteria: Library exports asyncIterableToReadableStream and readableStreamToAsyncIterable with full TypeScript types
Cancellation via AbortSignal closes both sides and surfaces CancellationError
Backpressure preserved: consumer-driven pull prevents unbounded memory growth in tests
Polyfill/adapters added for Node 16/18+, Deno, and browser harness with CI tests
Docs include two migration examples and a short troubleshooting section
Benchmarks show < 10% overhead vs minimal naive adapter on conservative workloads
comments: 2025-11-12 Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket created. Referencing prior interop work: ENG-4721 + ENG-21047. Core goal is to reduce customer support incidents where devs accidentally lose cancellation or see huge memory usage when bridging streams.

2025-11-14 Liam Chen: Spike finished. Implemented prototype for browser ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable that preserves pull() semantics via the stream reader. Observed a tricky edge: when a consumer abandons the iterator mid-pull, the underlying reader.lock() needs explicit release; otherwise subsequent consumers get a locked stream. Added a 'safeTee' option in the prototype.

2025-11-16 Design review (Nora Patel): Asked for clearer UX around teeing and multiple consumers. Recommended explicit error when multi-consume is attempted without tee: true. Also requested short doc snippet showing a retry pattern using resumeTokenHook.

2025-11-18 Engineering review (Diego Ramos): Benchmarks attached: basic adapter median latency +4.2% and memory peak +7% on small-chunk workload. Suggested adding earlyFlush option to trade throughput for token latency. Created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4892

2025-11-19 QA (Samir Gupta): Created test matrix and added flaky test that simulates abrupt network reset while converting ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable. Repro steps and fixture added under tests/interop/stream-raft. Noted that Node 16 adapter needs additional buffering to avoid early EOF in simulated proxy environment.
